events.title: Patrick Volkerding releases Slackware Linux
events.summary: Patrick Volkerding released Slackware 1.0 on July 17, 1993 — one of the earliest maintained Linux distributions.
events.about: Slackware prioritized simplicity and Unix-like purity — influencing how early Linux users installed servers and desktops. Volkerding has maintained it for decades as one of the longest-running distro projects.

narrative.whyChosen: Slackware is the oldest surviving Linux distribution still maintained by its founder.
narrative.whyImportant: It helped standardize early Linux packaging and installation practices.
narrative.problemSolved: Early Linux required manually assembling filesystems from [kernel] and GNU tools.

events.title: Windows NT 3.1 released
events.summary: Microsoft released Windows NT 3.1 on July 27, 1993 — a 32-bit operating system with the NT [kernel], [POSIX] subsystem, and Win32 [API].
events.about: NT brought preemptive multitasking, security ACLs, and Unicode to Windows — the lineage behind Windows XP, Server, and Azure hosts. Developers got a stable Win32 platform for servers and workstations separate from the [DOS]-based Windows 3.x line.

narrative.whyChosen: Windows NT was Microsoft's clean-slate 32-bit [OS] for servers and professionals.
narrative.whyImportant: The NT [kernel] still underpins modern Windows and enterprise deployments.
narrative.problemSolved: [DOS]-based Windows could not scale to servers, security, or heavy multitasking.
